title: 第二十章寻刀第十九章入局第十八章复仇
lines: 第二十章寻刀
宋焘在河南府待了一个月。一个月里，他每天都在街上走。他走遍了每一条巷子，看遍了每一个角落。他看见了卖菜的被收税的欺负，看见了拉车的被当兵的打，看见了寡妇被邻居指着脊梁骨骂。他看见了很多，比天书上写的多得多。天书上的故事，是写下来的，干干净净的，有开头，有结尾，有因果。人间的日子，是活出来的，乱七八糟的，没有开头，没有结尾，有因没果，有果没因。
他站在街边，看着一滩积水。水里映着他的脸，很瘦，很白，眼睛很亮，像两颗浸在溪水里的黑石子。他看了很久，忽然觉得那张脸很眼熟。像谁？像乔生？像张福？像商三官？像每一个他看过的人。
他摸了摸怀里的笔。笔还在，很轻，轻得像没有重量。
“你不能一直站着。”他对自己说。
他开始找一个人。一个能替他做的人。他不知道那个人是谁，不知道他在哪里，甚至不知道这世上有没有这样一个人。但他知道，他必须找到他。
宋焘去了府衙。府衙很大，门口站着两个差役，腰里挂着刀，脸上没有表情。宋焘站在对面街角，看着进出的人。穿官服的，穿绸缎的，穿布衣的，穿破衫的。每一个人他都会在心里问一句：是你吗？
第一天，他看见一个官员，骑着高头大马，前呼后拥。衙役在前面开道，百姓纷纷避让。他下了马，走进衙门，头也不回。宋焘看着他的背影，摇了摇头。不是。
第二天，他看见一个师爷，从侧门出来，手里拎着一个食盒。他低着头，走得很快，像是怕被人看见。走到街角，钻进一辆马车里，走了。宋焘看着马车消失在巷口，摇了摇头。不是。
第三天，他看见一个捕快，从衙门里出来，腰里挂着铁链。他走得很慢，一边走一边剔牙。走到街边，踢了一个乞丐一脚，骂了一句，走了。宋焘看着他的背影，摇了摇头。不是。
他在府衙门口站了三天。三天里，他看了上百个人，没有一个是。
宋焘去了集市。集市很热闹，人挤人，肩碰肩。卖菜的，卖肉的，卖布的，卖杂货的，扯着嗓子喊。算命的，耍猴的，说书的，拉琴的，围成一圈。宋焘站在人群里，看着来来往往的人。每一个人的脸，他都会仔细看。看他的眼睛，看他的手，看他的步子。
第一天，他看见一个汉子，生得五大三粗，手里提着一把杀猪刀。他走到肉摊前，一刀下去，骨头都剁碎了。宋焘看着他，心里想：你心里有火吗？汉子收了钱，笑嘻嘻地走了。宋焘摇了摇头。不是。
第二天，他看见一个书生，穿着洗得发白的长衫，手里拿着一本书。他站在书摊前，翻了一本又一本，一本也没买。书摊老板不耐烦了，说：“不买就别翻了！”书生红着脸，放下书，走了。宋焘看着他，心里想：你心里有火吗？书生低着头，走得很快，像是怕被人看见。宋焘摇了摇头。不是。
第三天，他看见一个老人，挑着一担柴，从山上下来。他的背驼了，腿弯了，每一步都很慢。走到集市上，放下担子，等着人来买。等了半天，没人来。他舔了舔干裂的嘴唇，又把担子挑起来，走了。宋焘看着他，心里想：你心里有火吗？老人走了，背影越来越小。宋焘摇了摇头。不是。
他在集市站了三天。三天里，他看了几百个人，没有一个是。
宋焘去了城隍庙。不是他的庙，是河南府的城隍庙。比他那座大得多，但也破得多。屋顶漏了，墙皮掉了，神像上的金漆都剥落了，露出里面的泥胎。庙里没有香火，地上落了一层灰。一个老庙祝坐在门口晒太阳，眼睛闭着，不知道是睡着了还是醒着。
宋焘走进去，站在神像前。神像的脸已经看不清了，但他知道，那里面住着一个城隍，和他一样。他站在那里，站了很久。想说什么，又不知道该说什么。最后他问了一句：“你在吗？”
没有人回答。神像还是那副样子，似笑非笑，似看非看。宋焘等了一会儿，转身走了。走到门口，老庙祝睁开眼睛，看了他一眼。
“你找谁？”老庙祝问。
“不找谁。”宋焘说。
“那你来庙里做什么？”
宋焘想了想。“找人。”
老庙祝笑了。牙掉了好几颗，笑得很丑。“找谁？”
“找一个能做事的人。”
老庙祝看着他，看了很久。然后他指了指外面。“你去城东看看。那里有一个人，天天对着尸体说话。有人说他是疯子，有人说他是好人。你去看看，他是不是你要找的人。”
宋焘的心跳了一下。他谢了老庙祝，转身走了。走了几步，又停下来，回头看了一眼。老庙祝已经闭上眼睛了，像一尊泥塑。
城东有一片乱坟岗。坟岗旁边有一座破房子，门上挂着一块匾，写着“义庄”两个字。匾很旧，字都模糊了，但还能认出来。宋焘站在门口，没有进去。他在等。等天黑。
天黑的时候，义庄里亮起一盏灯。灯很暗，火苗一跳一跳的，像随时会灭。宋焘推开门，走进去。一股腐臭味扑面而来，混着草药和石灰的气味。角落里有一只猫，蹲在阴影里，眼睛绿莹莹的，盯着他看。墙根有窸窸窣窣的声音，是老鼠在啃什么东西。

Chapter 20 Looking for the Knife
Song Tao stayed in Henan Mansion for a month. He walked the streets every day for a month. He walked down every alley and looked around every corner. He saw the vegetable seller being bullied by the tax collectors, the cart puller being beaten by the soldiers, and the widow being pointed at the spine and scolded by her neighbors. He saw a lot, much more than what was written in the Book of Heaven. The stories in the Book of Heaven are written down, clean, with a beginning, an end, and cause and effect. The days in the world are lived and messy, with no beginning and no end. There are causes but no effects, and effects but no causes.
He stood on the street, looking at a puddle of water. His face reflected in the water was very thin and white, with bright eyes, like two black pebbles soaked in the stream. He looked at it for a long time, and suddenly felt that the face looked familiar. Like who? Like Qiao Sheng? Like Zhang Fu? Like Shang Sanguan? Like everyone he's ever seen.
He touched the pen in his arms. The pen is still there, very light, as light as weightless.
"You can't stand all the time," he said to himself.
He started looking for someone. Someone who could do it for him. He didn't know who that person was, didn't know where he was, or even whether there was such a person in the world. But he knew he had to find him.
Song Tao went to the government office. The government office was very large, and there were two guards standing at the door, with knives hanging on their waists and expressionless faces. Song Tao stood on the opposite street corner, watching the people going in and out. Those who wear official uniforms, those who wear silk and satin, those who wear cloth, and those who wear rags. Everyone will ask in his heart: Is it you?
On the first day, he saw an official riding a tall horse, cheering in front and behind him. The government officials cleared the way in front, and the people gave way one after another. He got off his horse and walked into the Yamen without looking back. Song Tao looked at his back and shook his head. no.
The next day, he saw a master coming out of the side door, carrying a food box in his hand. He lowered his head and walked quickly, as if he was afraid of being seen. He walked to the corner, got into a carriage, and left. Song Tao watched the carriage disappear at the entrance of the alley and shook his head. no.
On the third day, he saw a policeman coming out of the Yamen with a chain hanging from his waist. He walked slowly, picking his teeth as he went. He walked to the street, kicked a beggar, cursed, and left. Song Tao looked at his back and shook his head. no.
He stood at the gate of the government office for three days. In three days, he saw hundreds of people and found no one.
Song Tao went to the market. The market is very lively, crowded and crowded. Vegetable sellers, meat sellers, cloth sellers, and groceries sellers shouted at the top of their lungs. Fortune tellers, monkey charmers, storytellers, and piano players formed a circle. Song Tao stood in the crowd, watching the people coming and going. He would look carefully at everyone's face. Look at his eyes, look at his hands, look at his steps.
On the first day, he saw a man, tall and thick, holding a butcher's knife in his hand. He walked to the meat stall and chopped the bones into pieces with one slash of his knife. Song Tao looked at him and thought to himself: Are you angry in your heart? The man took the money and left with a smile. Song Tao shook his head. no.
The next day, he saw a scholar wearing a washed white gown and holding a book in his hand. He stood in front of the bookstall, flipping through one book after another, but didn't buy any of them. The bookstall owner became impatient and said, "If you don't buy it, don't read it!" The scholar blushed, put down the book, and left. Song Tao looked at him and thought to himself: Are you angry in your heart? The scholar lowered his head and walked quickly, as if he was afraid of being seen. Song Tao shook his head. no.
On the third day, he saw an old man coming down from the mountain carrying a load of firewood. His back was hunched, his legs were bent, and every step was slow. Go to the market, put down your burden, and wait for people to buy. After waiting for a long time, no one came. He licked his chapped lips, picked up the burden again, and left. Song Tao looked at him and thought to himself: Are you angry in your heart? The old man left, and his figure became smaller and smaller. Song Tao shook his head. no.
He stood in the market place for three days. In three days, he saw hundreds of people and found no one.
Song Tao went to the Chenghuang Temple. It's not his temple, it's the City God's Temple in Henan Prefecture. It was much bigger than his one, but also much worse. The roof is leaking, the wall coverings are falling off, and the gold paint on the statues has peeled off, exposing the mud tires inside. There was no incense in the temple, and there was a layer of ashes on the ground. An old Miao Zhu was sitting at the door, basking in the sun, with his eyes closed, not sure whether he was asleep or awake.
Song Tao walked in and stood in front of the statue. The face of the statue could no longer be seen clearly, but he knew that there lived a city god just like him. He stood there for a long time. I want to say something, but I don’t know what to say. Finally he asked: "Are you there?"
No one answered. The statue still looks like that, smiling but not smiling, looking but not looking. Song Tao waited for a while, turned around and left. When he reached the door, Lao Miaozhu opened his eyes and glanced at him.
"Who are you looking for?" Lao Miaozhu asked.
"I'm not looking for anyone." Song Tao said.
"Then what are you doing in the temple?"
Song Tao thought for a while. "Find someone."
Lao Miaozhu smiled. I lost several teeth and my smile looked ugly. "Who are you looking for?"
"Find someone who can do something."
Lao Miaozhu looked at him for a long time. Then he pointed outside. "Go to the east of the city and have a look. There is a man there who talks to corpses every day. Some say he is a madman, others say he is a good man. Go and see if he is the person you are looking for."
Song Tao's heart skipped a beat. He thanked the old man for his blessing, turned around and left. After walking a few steps, he stopped and looked back. Lao Miaozhu had closed his eyes, like a clay sculpture.
There is a mass grave in the east of the city. There is a dilapidated house next to the tomb, with a plaque hanging on the door that reads "Yizhuang". The plaque is very old and the words are blurred, but it is still legible. Song Tao stood at the door and did not go in. He is waiting. Wait until dark.
When it gets dark, a lamp lights up in the yizhuang. The light was very dim, and the flames were jumping up and down, as if they would go out at any moment. Song Tao
